 By Claire Wang | cwang@scng.com PUBLISHED: November 3, 2026 at 8:26 PM PST | UPDATED: November 3, 2026 at 11:03 PM PST Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... 
 Ben Davis, Erin Spivey, Casey McKeon and Taryn Palumbo continue to lead a crowded race for Huntington Beach City Council as more returns are posted Tuesday night after polls closed.
 Close behind the four leaders were Pat Burns, Andrew Gruel, Brenda Glim and Brian Thienes.
 Brian Burley, Rosaline Price and Amory Hanson trailed far behind.
 Eleven candidates were competing for four open seats on the Huntington Beach City Council.
 LIVE ELECTION RESULTS: See a chart of the latest vote counts 
 Incumbents Burns , McKeon and Gruel are looking to hold onto their seats. For Gruel, this was a first campaign; he was appointed to his seat in 2025 when Tony Strickland took his state Senate seat.
 But with Councilmember Gracey Van Der Mark running instead for state office, there is at least one new face guaranteed from the crowded field of challengers: Burley , Davis , Glim , Hanson , Palumbo , Price , Spivey and Thienes .
 Looking to shake up the seven-member conservative council, four candidates have been running as the progressive Surf City 4 slate: Davis, a civil rights attorney; Glim, a medical education actor; Palumbo, an attorney and nonprofit leader; and Spivey, a former librarian who successfully sued the city over its library book restriction policy.
 They occupied three of the top four spots as the first batch of votes were counted.
 “We feel pretty good about our initial returns,” Spivey said Tuesday night. “Obviously, our platform is resonating with people who are looking for a return to normalcy, a City Council with no drama and an end to culture war issues.”
 Three conservatives have been running as an opposing slate, Team HB: Burns, McKeon and Thienes, a local business owner.
 Burley, a system administrator at USC, is also vying for California’s 42nd Congressional District against incumbent Rep. Robert Garcia, D-Long Beach. Hanson, a historian, is running for City Council for the sixth time.
